A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IRIS and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The moved references and renumbered appendix content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original inverse-rendering, novel-view synthesis, relighting, and CRF experiments, including synthetic quantitative results, real-scene visualizations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports revised ablation results, an additional qualitative comparison, and training times.

M1.justification: The CRF representation, emitter detection, HDR restoration, shading baking, and alternating optimization remain unchanged. Equations (1) and (8) make basis-weight and albedo-alignment indices explicit without documenting a different algorithm or loss mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanNet++ and FIPT scene coverage and retain constant/varying-exposure and CRF evaluations. The added real-scene comparison in Figure 15 uses an already represented conference-room setting and existing tasks.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 15 adds an evaluated NeILF++ comparator and includes Li et al. in this real-scene decomposition/relighting comparison. NeILF++ was discussed but not shown as an evaluated comparator in v2. Existing quantitative comparator sets, including I2-SDF in Table 5, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes from cumulative component additions to individual component-removal controls. It also adds emission-mask IoU and changes the reported CRF/emission error metric from MSE to L2. Main benchmark protocols remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that otherwise identical experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 revises the component ablations and incorporates updated versions of the loss ablations previously reported in v2 Table 8, with additional emission measurements. These refine existing component-validation questions. The CRF/exposure sensitivity study, albedo-initialization visualization, and failure case are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3 does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Ablation results are replaced: Table 3's full-model material PSNRs change from 23.22/17.52/20.35 to 22.33/17.92/21.38, and the former Table 8 loss-ablation values also change. Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 retain their values. V3 adds Figure 15 and training times of 57/298/50 minutes for IRIS/NeILF/FIPT. The revised ablations do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The rendering and factorized-light-transport derivations, BRDF definitions, and assumptions are retained. Added indices and numbering of an existing rendering equation are not substantive mathematical changes. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about recovering HDR lighting, materials, and CRFs from LDR images and enabling realistic relighting and object insertion.

C2.justification: V3 removes v2 Section 11's explanation that erroneous albedo/emission can conceal unnatural CRFs in photometric loss, and its discussion of the ambiguities addressed by albedo regularization. The limitations concerning saturated emitter masks and global CRF modeling remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix B newly reports 57 minutes of training on one RTX 4090 and comparative baseline timings. This adds resource and implementation information without establishing a hardware or training-budget change. Existing implementation details and the promise to release code and data remain.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 57 works and retain the same substantive positioning against prior inverse-rendering and CRF methods. The new NeILF++ evaluation changes empirical comparison coverage, not the stated novelty or research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and notation edits, moves references before the supplement, and changes supplementary section numbers 8–14 to appendices A–G. It also revises the additional-ablation introduction and removes the loss-ablation discussion; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 is redesigned with removal-based rows and additional metric columns, while the separate loss-ablation Table 8 disappears. V3 adds Figure 15, renumbers the former Figures 15–18, and reflows supplementary material. Existing figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Individual-removal controls in Table 3, the additional real-scene baseline comparison in Figure 15, and hardware/runtime disclosure modestly strengthen validation and practical transparency. The benefit is limited by unexplained ablation-value/metric revisions, Section 6.4's retained references to the old cumulative rows, and removal of the loss-ablation interpretation. Main benchmark performance and scientific claims remain unchanged.
